The standard chain uses purity by choice, on two grounds (Ref. [41], R1.8). First, mixing background treatments inside one covariance is worse than either consistent choice: inserting a lateral-band block built with negative-weight subtraction into a central and vertical set built with purity subtraction is a mismatch, not an upgrade. Second, switching would have required rerunning every unfold above and would have invalidated the flux-corrected covariance, which had just been chosen for use. This consequence, not the computing cost, decided the choice. The background treatment has been revisited in two dimensions: the closure test below is its result, and the 2D result and its covariance use the refined estimator. For the five-dimensional central value, which still uses purity, the revisit is open.
